title: Re-review cadence: refresh lessons past their lastReviewed window
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Lesson content can become outdated as language idioms, best practices, or documentation evolve. The lastReviewed date on each lesson drives a re-review cadence that ensures no lesson drifts past its review window unchecked. This is the sustainability mechanism that keeps the corpus accurate over time.
objective: Identify all lessons whose lastReviewed date has passed the review window, re-review each for technical accuracy and pedagogy currency, update lastReviewed on passing lessons, and log issues found for any that require content updates.
acceptanceCriteria: All lessons with a lastReviewed date older than the review window (defined in the pedagogy guide) are identified.
Each identified lesson is re-reviewed for technical accuracy (idiomatic and correct for the current language version) and pedagogy currency (still beginner-appropriate, no broken links in citations).
Lessons that pass re-review have their lastReviewed date updated in the schema.
Lessons that fail re-review are flagged with specific issues and a follow-up task is created for each fix.
A summary of the re-review cycle (lessons reviewed, pass/fail, issues found) is committed to the maintenance log.
output: A committed maintenance log documenting the re-review cycle outcomes, updated lastReviewed dates in lesson files, and any follow-up fix tasks created.
